title:
Install FriRSS
on your server
intro: Prepare FreshRSS, install FriRSS, then connect the two. Follow this guide to your first read.
prereqText: FriRSS displays articles from your FreshRSS instance. Before you start, prepare these three things.
dockerText: Run the official image. Port 8080 on your host maps to port 80 in the container; /app/data stores the database and encryption keys.
composeText: Save this as compose.yaml in an empty directory, then run the commands below. Keep the frirss-data directory: it holds your instance data.
unraidText: Open the Apps tab in Unraid Community Applications, search for FriRSS and install its template. Check the host port and persistent /app/data mapping before starting.
imageNote: Also available on Docker Hub as fripix/frirss. Official images support amd64 and arm64.
accountText: Once the container is running, open this address on the Docker host, or use that host’s address from another device. Create the first FriRSS account immediately: it becomes the administrator. Registration then closes and can be reopened in Preferences → Administration.
connectText: This time, use your FreshRSS credentials. They are separate from the FriRSS account you just created.
privateText: The proxy blocks private addresses by default. Explicitly allow your FreshRSS hostname or IP with PROXY_INTERNAL_HOSTS. Replace the example address with your actual host; do not disable the protection globally.
privateUsage: Docker: add -e PROXY_INTERNAL_HOSTS=192.168.1.20 before the image name. Compose: remove the # in front of the PROXY_INTERNAL_HOSTS line and replace the address with your FreshRSS’s. Recreate the container after changing it.
nextTitle: A few things for a lasting setup

notes.title: Keep your data
notes.text: Back up /app/data using the official SQLite snapshot procedure or encrypted export. Copying only a live frirss.db file is not a reliable backup.

notes.title: Give it HTTPS
notes.text: For remote access, use an HTTPS reverse proxy; do not expose the container port directly to the internet. For AI translations, allow read and send timeouts of at least 120 seconds.

notes.title: Update deliberately
notes.text: Read the release notes, back up your data, then pull the new image and recreate the container. The official README remains the reference for evolving configuration.

commandsNote: The official README remains the reference if an option or a command changes.
methodHint: Choose your method. Creating your account and connecting FreshRSS work the same way afterwards.

prerequisites.title: An accessible FreshRSS instance
prerequisites.text: Keep its address and your username handy.

prerequisites.title: API access enabled
prerequisites.text: In FreshRSS: Settings → Authentication → Allow API access.

prerequisites.title: An API password
prerequisites.text: Set it in FreshRSS under Settings → Profile. You will use it to connect FriRSS.

connectionFields.label: FreshRSS address
connectionFields.text: The URL of your instance, for example https://rss.example.com.

connectionFields.label: FreshRSS username
connectionFields.text: The account whose subscriptions you want to read.

connectionFields.label: API password
connectionFields.text: The password set in your FreshRSS profile during preparation.

readyTitle: Your feeds are ready to read.
readyText: Choose your layout, your theme and your first article. You can fine-tune the rest as you go.

hosting.title: Grow your installation
hosting.intro: FriRSS works with its built-in SQLite database. Redis is an optional addition for faster reading and shared caching across devices.
hosting.baselineText: Accounts, preferences and configuration live in the built-in database. Back up your FriRSS data: no additional database service is required.

options.name: Redis
options.text: A shared cache for article lists, extracted articles and AI results. It avoids repeating the same work for each device or user.
options.advice: A useful addition for faster repeat visits. FriRSS also works without Redis.
options.setup: Connect your Redis service with REDIS_URL. Background prefetching is enabled separately with CACHE_SYNC_INTERVAL, which requires Redis.

formLabel: The FriRSS form for adding a FreshRSS server, with the server URL, the FreshRSS user and the API password.

privacy.title: Privacy and security
privacy.intro: FriRSS runs on your server and keeps only what it needs. Here is what it stores, where, and what leaves your installation.

groups.title: On your server
items: A single SQLite database, in /app/data: accounts, synced preferences and instance settings.
Your FreshRSS API password is never saved: FriRSS keeps only the login token, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and never sends it to the browser.
Your articles stay in FreshRSS. Without Redis, the text of extracted articles is not kept.

groups.title: In your browser
items: The session, the preferences that belong to this screen and the feeds’ icons.
Articles and images prepared for offline reading, which you can clear at any time.

groups.title: What leaves your installation
items: To your FreshRSS server: always, that is what FriRSS is for.
To the articles’ websites: only if full articles are turned on. They are off by default.
To an AI provider: only if the administrator turns it on. The article’s title and text are sent to it.
To your single sign-on (SSO) provider: only if the administrator turns it on.
Article images are loaded by the browser from their own site, as in any RSS reader.

privacy.telemetryText: FriRSS has no analytics, no crash reporting and no update check: it contacts no server of its author.
privacy.keyNote: The key that encrypts the tokens is kept in the same database. Protect and back up the /app/data folder like a password.

vars.title: Environment variables
vars.intro: All are optional except TZ, already set. In compose.yaml, remove the # in front of a line to turn it on; with docker run, add ‑e NAME=value before the image name. Then recreate the container.
vars.note: Optional: remove the # in front of a line to turn it on (see the table).

rows.name: TZ
rows.text: The container’s time zone, for dates and logs. Example: Europe/London.

rows.name: PUID, PGID
rows.text: User and group FriRSS runs as. The data folder is taken over in their name on start.

rows.name: FRIRSS_BASE_URL
rows.text: FriRSS’s public address. Recommended behind a reverse proxy; also fixes the single sign-on (OIDC) redirect addresses.

rows.name: PROXY_INTERNAL_HOSTS
rows.text: Private hosts FriRSS may reach, comma-separated. Needed when FreshRSS sits on your local network or a Docker network.

rows.name: PROXY_REWRITES
rows.text: Reach FreshRSS over the internal network instead of its public address: public address=internal address, comma-separated.

rows.name: CORS_ORIGIN
rows.text: Allowed origins, only when the interface and the server are served separately.

rows.name: REDIS_URL
rows.text: Turns the cache on: lists shown at once, background pre-fetch, extracted articles and AI results shared by the whole instance.

rows.name: CACHE_ARTICLES_PER_FEED
rows.text: Articles kept in the cache per feed.

rows.name: CACHE_TTL
rows.text: Lifetime of a cache entry, in seconds.

rows.name: CACHE_SYNC_INTERVAL
rows.text: Background pre-fetch, every N minutes. 0 turns it off; needs REDIS_URL.

rows.name: CACHE_SYNC_ACTIVE_DAYS
rows.text: Only pre-fetches for accounts seen in the last N days.

rows.name: FRIRSS_REFRESH_MAX_FEEDS
rows.text: Feeds refreshed on each click on Refresh.

rows.name: FRIRSS_PROXY_RATE_LIMIT
rows.text: Requests per account per minute, one budget shared by the proxy, article extraction and AI. 0 removes the limit.

rows.name: FRIRSS_DATA_DIR
rows.text: SQLite database folder, inside the container.
